name: Toon shading
one_line: 3D forms rendered with a few flat tonal steps and a clean outline, like a cel drawing
summary: Smooth lighting on a 3D form is collapsed into a handful of flat tones, with a hard highlight and a line around the silhouette. It reads as animation cel, comic or game art, and keeps a model legible and graphic at small sizes. Step count, outline weight and whether the line holds steady as the camera moves decide whether it feels crafted or cheap.

routes.one_line: Stepped ramp material and an inverted-hull outline in a browser 3D scene

steps.does: Render the model with a stepped tone ramp and back-face outline, redrawn from t on each seek

limits: Three.js evidence is a render-once-per-seek scene; no toon material or outline is tested
Outline width stability under camera movement is yours to check
Evidence ran in a Linux container with a stand-in Chromium

routes.one_line: Toon-shaded scene with the outline found by an edge pass over depth and normals

steps.does: Detect edges on the rendered scene and draw the outline in screen space

limits: Postprocessing evidence covers bloom and chromatic aberration, not an edge or outline pass
Edge passes can flicker on thin geometry; check frames either side of a seek

routes.one_line: Render toon-shaded frames offline with the native renderer

steps.does: Build the scene with stepped shading and outline and render the frame sequence

limits: Blender evidence is one Workbench still; no EEVEE, Cycles or animation
Shader-based stepped shading does not export to other tools
